goal: Guide a participant through two Monday 90-minute sprints: validate Azure Cost Optimizer locally from 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM, then deploy the supplied curated web experience, validate Agent ACO, generate a report, and review a screenshot from 1:45 PM to 3:15 PM. OpenAPI and MCP prompt agents are optional bonus work.

sprint_1.outcome: validated local product and authorized evidence or an exact blocker

sprint_2.outcome: curated hosted web, validated Agent ACO answer, generated report, and screenshot evidence or one exact blocker

interaction_model.participant_interface: natural-language prompts through ACO Workshop Builder
interaction_model.step_execution: One requested numbered README step per turn; kickoff authorizes preparation only. End the turn at each checkpoint and wait for the next numbered step request.
interaction_model.recommended_permissions: Manual or Default Approvals; Allow all, Bypass Approvals and Autopilot off. Tool permissions do not grant Azure or spend approval.
interaction_model.raw_command_disclosure: Only on explicit participant request, direct interactive necessity, or one exact blocked recovery path.
interaction_model.rule: The Builder may execute an operation only when the delivery contract does not require approval or after matching explicit approval for that exact action and scope.

security_control_tag.rule: Never set a bypass or exception value unless the participant's subscription owner explicitly approves that exact value. The tag does not replace identity, authorization, TLS, or data protection.

checks: producer bundle receipt or extracted participant tree validation
preparation.participant_integrity: The facilitator verifies the downloaded ZIP against its external receipt. An extracted participant tree has no producer-only manifest/receipt; structure validation is not archive authenticity verification.
preparation.remediation: ACO Workshop Builder explains each missing item and obtains explicit approval before one organization-approved installation at a time.

guide: README is the only root Markdown guide
separate solution tour and hands-on workshop
Manual permissions and one numbered step per turn
four architecture views: solution overview, shared platform, Azure deployment, data flow
bordered sanitized product screenshots with service evidence/bar and resource-group evidence/pie
future Microsoft 365 channels clearly labeled unimplemented
live: portal parity or explicit pending state

query_processing_units.approximate_cost: one QPU per month of data queried

throttle_policy.no_snapshot_outcome: collection fails and the dashboard is blocked until the retry time
throttle_policy.prior_snapshot_outcome: previous validated evidence is returned unchanged and keeps its own status; the attempt is disclosed as cost_source_status deferred-throttled with failed_source, retry_at and one replaced throttled receipt
throttle_policy.degraded_cached_meaning: a non-throttle collection failure with a prior snapshot; marks summary and data health degraded
throttle_policy.retry_circuit: further provider calls for that scope and period are suppressed until retry_at passes
session_guidance: Prefer the This month window during the session.
Stagger refreshes; simultaneous refreshes in one tenant exhaust the 12 QPU per 10 seconds budget first.
Each period is collected and cached separately.

limitations: Prompt instructions guide workshop pacing but are not a deterministic permission enforcement boundary.

Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams publication requires a separate authenticated adapter or verified Foundry-agent publication path, tenant approval, supported UI mapping and cost review; it is not included in workshop completion.
Cost data can be delayed and current-period values can change.
Cost Management Query quotas are shared per tenant, so other activity in the same tenant can throttle a participant who has made no recent request.
Advisor savings are estimates and can overlap.
The workshop is not a production security, compliance, high-availability, or disaster-recovery certification.
Public network access is a workshop option; private networking is a separate architecture initiative.
